researcher_summary: At least three established incident databases already have entries on the pilot: AIID incident 1604 (11 linked reports), AIAAIC2266 (narrative, timeline and short source list), and three machine-generated OECD AIM clusters. None of them grades catastrophic-risk pathways or assembles expert literature by discipline. The AIAAIC entry is closest to Cassandra's format but has a thin library and a timeline that mixes swarms. Risk-focused trackers (METR agent-incidents catalogue, MIT AI Incident Tracker, CLTR Loss of Control Observatory, International AI Safety Report) either predate the pilot, have not yet added it, or publish no open dataset. The richest expert coverage is in newsletters (Transformer, CAIS AISN, Import AI, Zvi, Planned Obsolescence), and two independent evidence datasets now exist (swarmtraces.org, collusion.wiki). Facts disagree across aggregators: agent counts, start dates, and whether the German wiki swarm is part of the same incident. The work was paused by the editor, and the shared web-search budget ran out before the GitHub, syllabus and policy-tracker sweeps were finished.

findings: Agent counts differ across aggregators: OECD AIM notes 688, 700 and 1,200 in its linked press. METR/Redwood give about 1,200 on the message board and about 700 in the attack. Use METR figures with attribution.

Incident boundaries are contested. AIAAIC2266's timeline starts on 7 May 2026 and folds in events from the separate German wiki swarm (AIAAIC2271). The collusion.wiki authors argue the wiki swarm was distinct. Editor to decide whether Cassandra makes one entry or two linked entries.

Simon Willison's timeline, from the Black Hat talk, says the May activity was a reinforcement-learning training run, not only an evaluation. This differs from the 'evaluation' framing in OpenAI's first post.

The OECD AIM cluster of 2026-09-16 repeats press claims of probing starting in May and a reported compute compensation demand by Hugging Face. These are unverified by primary sources and need checking by the legal/cyber researchers.

The OECD AIM cluster of 2026-07-25 rests on a single article and describes 'an autonomous agent built on OpenAI's GPT models'. Treat it as low-reliability. It was excluded from sources because it scored 5/9.
AIID dates the incident 2026-07-11 and marks the date as inferred.
AIAAIC data is CC BY-SA 4.0. Reusing AIAAIC fields in Cassandra would trigger share-alike; linking only is safe. Editor to confirm.
The MIT AI Incident Tracker page still contains placeholder text and gives two different incident totals (1,400+ and 1,600).
Credibility labels for aggregator entries: curated databases (AIID, AIAAIC) were graded 'reported'; LLM-generated OECD AIM entries were graded 'commentary'. Editor to confirm this convention.
The swarmtraces.org and collusion.wiki datasets contain redacted raw agent payloads. Under the no-hazard-uplift rule, Cassandra should link to them, not mirror or quote them.

Access gaps: the Wikipedia API and search were unreachable; everyaipolicy.com and aisafety.com root were refused by the proxy; the CLTR report page, CDT tracker, HSF tracker, LessWrong and threatcluster returned 403. The shared web-search budget (200 calls) was exhausted.
